The operating system is literally for autistic robots, but I'll keep trying.

Part of the hook with Linux is if you're an old enough IT person to have supported and loved DOS, and still drop to the command prompt frequently in Windows, you tend to pick up the billion CLI commands needed to maintain a Linux system. If you run Linux with a GUI, you tend to never really learn Linux that well. A 'Desktop' build of Linux are for those who are looking for a basic OS to install when you don't want MS or don't have a license key for Windows. It's great for laptops and whatnot when you want to browse the web, watch Youtube, etc. But not for a server.

If you're looking to run a server at home, there is literally nothing better than a Server edition of a Linux build. I've always been a Debian/Ubuntu person myself. Redhat/CentOS are more for the Corp environment. Home users who wish to run a web server, especially a Do-It-All Media server, or whatever, just stick with Ubuntu Server. The 'Ask Ubuntu' forums are a goldmine for help and how-to.
